name: All-Terrain Vehicle
description: A motor-driven, off-road recreational vehicle designed by its manufacturer for cross-country travel, explicitly including motorcycles and other two-wheeled vehicles, so an off-road electric dirt bike is one. Registered with the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife. Defined by Maine Revised Statutes Title 12 §13001(3) and regulated by §13152 to §13157-A.
restrictions: Originally designed by the manufacturer for cross-country travel; includes motorcycles and other two- or three-wheeled vehicles, with no limit on power or speed
Registered with the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, except when ridden only on land the operator owns or leases
Children under 10 may not operate one; riders 10 to 15 must complete an approved ATV training course and be accompanied by an adult, except on family land or a training site
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear protective headgear
Ridden on another's land only with the landowner's permission, which is presumed on designated state-approved ATV trails
Kept off public ways used by cars and their sidewalks, except to cross within 500 yards, on posted ATV-access routes, and in a few other narrow cases
Barred from controlled-access highways and their rights-of-way except at approved crossings and trail segments
